I am a 50-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with 30 years of experience. My family has two people and 12 mu of land. I rely on well irrigation because surface water is unreliable here on the North China Plain. Over three decades, I have learned that the wheat-maize rotation is the most reliable system for my main land — it gives me two crops a year and steady food and income. I plant 9 mu in this rotation and keep 3 mu for cotton because cotton prices have been decent and the cash helps with household expenses, but I do not plant more because with only two of us the weeding, pruning, and constant spraying are too much labor. For wheat, I use improved varieties like luyuan502 or jimai22 because they resist lodging and yield steadily around 1000 jin per mu. I rotary till before autumn sowing and apply compound fertilizer as basal, then topdress with urea at green-up in spring. I irrigate four times — winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and grain filling — because the well water is there and it protects the yield. For summer maize, I use hybrid seed like denghai605 because the hybrids produce bigger ears and tolerate our summer storms better. I plant directly into the wheat stubble with no tillage to save the crucial days between wheat harvest and maize sowing in June; maize only needs two irrigations at tasseling and filling. For cotton, I rotary till in April, sow improved varieties, and irrigate three times, but the real work is pest control — I spray every ten days or so against bollworm, aphids, and mites, about fifteen times total. These are the practices that have worked for me and my neighbors year after year.
